clauses.label: sole paragraph
clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
by section 1 of the Act of August 1,  
1914, 38 Stat. 609, 623 (U.S.C. title 19,  
sec. 2), it is ordered that the designation  
of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port  
of entry in Customs Collection District  
No. 31 (Alaska), be, and it is hereby,  
revoked.
This order shall become effective at  
the close of business January 15, 1941.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 8639 of January 14, 1941 (6 FR 455, Federal Register issue of January 17, 1941) revokes the designation of Unalaska, Alaska, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District No. 31 (Alaska) and states "This order shall become effective at" "the close of business January 15, 1941." The revocation is a one-time act with a stated effective moment; it was performed and the command exhausted at the close of business on January 15, 1941. The loss of port-of-entry status is a surviving consequence of that executed act, not a continuing command. No instrument held in the repository revokes, amends or restores the designation by executive order. The working text is the official Federal Register page text (machine-extracted from the PDF, OCR), not an authenticated transcription.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists: the order is the revocation itself and states its own effective moment, the close of business January 15, 1941, so nothing can precede that moment. The packet's later-event chain is empty, the three machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes covering 1937 onward) return zero hits, and the bounded held-text search found no later order citing it by number. A later restoration of the port designation by an executive order would be a separate instrument that would not revive this one; none is held.","independent_command_check":"There is no independent command, delegation or continuing instruction. The only operative content is the revocation of the designation of Unalaska, and the order's own effective-date sentence fixes when it takes effect.","savings_check":"The order has no savings clause. The consequence, that Unalaska is no longer a designated customs port of entry in District No. 31, is a surviving effect of an executed act, not a continuing command of the order, and no held source shows any pending duty under it.","scope_check":"The packet inventory has one clause, the operative paragraph with the effective-date sentence (characters 2351 to 2733 of the registered text). I confirmed it against the whole held order: heading, the single operative sentence invoking section 1 of the Act of August 1, 1914 (38 Stat. 609, 623; 19 U.S.C. 2), the effective-date sentence, signature, date and filing line. The effective-date sentence is part of the same clause and fixes its end. No other clause exists."}
